{{Set infobox |name=Premiere (Japanese) |image=Premiere-Japanese-box.png |publisher=[[Decipher]] / [[Takara]] |era=[[:Category:Decipher sets|Decipher]] (1995–2001) |released=April 1997 |cards=324 (162 Light, 162 Dark) |code=GEMP set 1301 |country=Japan |language=Japanese |next=[[A New Hope (Japanese)]] |related=[[Premiere Limited]] · [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] }} '''Premiere (Japanese)''' (基本カード) is the Japanese-language edition of [[Premiere Limited]]. [[Takara]] published it in Japan in April 1997 as スターウォーズコレクションカードゲーム. It has 324 black-border cards, 162 Light Side and 162 Dark Side, 108 of each rarity. Decipher and Takara announced the partnership in December 1996. Steve Stanley, Decipher Senior Vice President and General Counsel, visited Tokyo for Takara's introduction of the set. Takara demonstrated it at the Tokyo Toy Show, 19–23 March 1997, at Tokyo Big Sight. The first three days were trade only. The last two days were open to the public. Takara's gameplay demonstrations had standing room only. Hirohisa Satoh, Jr., President of Takara Ltd., hosted the display. Takara pre-sold more than 80 percent of the print run before street date. Takara was translating the Tournament Kit. Japan was placed in the newly created Ord Mantell region on Decipher's tournament locator. A Japanese champion was expected to compete at the [[1997 Decipher World Championship]]. Takara could not ship the Japanese cards outside Japan. The English Limited set is the 1st expansion of Star Wars CCG. This printing translates that 324-card pool. GEMP loads the Japanese faces as set 1301. English-language packs from [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] through [[Endor]] were sold in Japan with a Takara overlabel on the pack. Poor translations led Japanese players to prefer the English-language cards. Takara and Decipher ended the partnership after Japanese Premiere, [[A New Hope (Japanese)|A New Hope]], [[Hoth (Japanese)|Hoth]], and the two Japanese two-player games. [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] has a separate Japanese product. Language editions are listed on [[Translations of SWCCG]]. == Packaging == Takara sold 15-card booster packs (MSRP ¥500) in 36-pack boxes. Each pack had 10 commons, 4 uncommons and 1 rare. 60-card starters (MSRP ¥1400) came in 12-deck displays. Each starter had 44 commons (22 per side), 14 uncommons (7 per side), 2 rares (1 per side) and a Japanese rulebook. {| class="wikitable" style="background:transparent; border:none;" |- style="background:transparent; border:none; vertical-align:bottom;" | style="border:none; text-align:center;" | [[File:Premiere-Japanese-box.png|260px|Japanese booster box]]

[[File:Premiere-Japanese-mains.png|1200px|Japanese Premiere main cards]] ''Vader, Tarkin, C-3PO, Han, Leia, Luke, Falcon and Obi-Wan'' == Memorabilia == Takara issued player's guides for the Japanese edition. One guide is a fold-out with a Light Side and Dark Side card line-up. {| class="wikitable" style="background:transparent; border:none;" |- style="background:transparent; vertical-align:top;" | style="border:none; text-align:center;" | [[File:Premiere-Japanese-Takara-guides-v2.png|280px|Takara Premiere player's guides]]

''Player's guide fold-out'' |} == Variants == Every Japanese [[Help Me Obi-Wan Kenobi (Japanese)|Help Me Obi-Wan Kenobi]] was printed on an Effect template instead of Interrupt. There was no corrected run, so it is not counted as a separate misprint. [[File:Premiere-Japanese-Help-Me-Obi-Wan-v2.png|320px|Japanese Help Me Obi-Wan Kenobi Effect template]] ''[[Help Me Obi-Wan Kenobi (Japanese)|Help Me Obi-Wan Kenobi]]: English Interrupt vs Japanese Effect template'' About half of the Japanese [[Corellian Corvette (Japanese)|Corellian Corvette]] copies have a stray mark in the printed title. The mark is part of the print-sheet layout. [[File:Premiere-Japanese-Corellian-Corvette-title-mark-v2.png|480px|Japanese Corellian Corvette title mark]] ''[[Corellian Corvette (Japanese)|Corellian Corvette]]: unmarked title and print-sheet mark'' == Other printings == English-language packs from [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] through [[Endor]] were sold in Japan with a Takara overlabel on the pack. [[File:Premiere-Japanese-Takara-overlabel-packs.png|520px|Takara overlabels on English A New Hope and Dagobah packs]] ''English [[A New Hope Limited|A New Hope]] and [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]] packs with Takara overlabels'' The English edition is [[Premiere Limited]]. The Japanese [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] followed in 1997. Japanese-language foil versions of some Premiere cards were packed in [[Reflections II: Expanding the Galaxy]] and [[Reflections III]]. They belong to those English products. Direct conflict often ends up in defeat for the Rebel fleet. It is now time to fight back. When brawn fails, brains must take over. The same cunning strategy that got [[Han Solo]] out of a tight situation in The Empire Strikes Back is at your disposal. The [[Landing Claw]] is a great tool to avoid a confrontation and put a stop to the Imperial control of the galaxy. This device permits you to create an "[[Undercover]]" starfighter. You block your opponent's Force drain without risking loosing Force in a battle. Of course, since you can only have two on the table at a time, you will still have to deploy other ships and attack, but now you have an ace in the hole. Not only do the ships present at the system engage the Imperial fleet, but your concealed starfighter "May detach at any time", thus increasing your power and ability total to give your opponent a run for his money. |rulings=* Show that the starfighter is attached by physically placing it on the opponent's capital starship. * While starfighter attached ('concealed'):The starfighter and cards aboard it are inactive (except for [[Homing Beacon]] and the [[Landing Claw]] itself).Prevents opponent from Force draining.If the capital starship is lost, the starfighter is also lost.The capital starship 'carries' the starfighter, the starfighter is not considered to be moving.If the capital starship lands, the starfighter remains attached.If the capital starship is landed when the starfighter detaches (or [[Landing Claw]] is canceled), the starfighter becomes landed there if possible, otherwise it is lost. * When the starfighter detaches (or [[Landing Claw]] is canceled), the starfighter returns to normal (is no longer attached/'concealed'). * Starfighter may either detach as a top level action, or when the capital starship is about to move (after destination has been specified and its movement cost has been paid). * Although an attached Light starship blocks Dark's Force drains, it does not prevent Dark from controlling a system (e.g. Dark can cancel [[Cloud City Celebration]] while a Light starship is attached). * [[Portable Scanner]] |canceled_by=* [[Captain Godherdt]] * [[Ghhhk & Those Rebels Won't Escape Us]] * [[Homing Beacon]] * [[Those Rebels Won't Escape Us]] }}

Text: “If you have deployed a site with exactly two [Dark Side] (and no other locations), deploy a battleground site. Place Interrupt in Lost Pile.” '''What changed:''' “unless you have deployed a site with "Palace" in title” became “unless you have deployed Imperial Square or a site with "Palace" in title”; “may deploy up to three Effects” became “deploy up to three Effects”. *: [[File:V12-D-slipslidingaway-20201014-changes.png|frameless|upright=2.6|alt=Before and after]] ''Before (left) and after (right): cropped from the published images.'' * '''PC-E2''' ([[Slip Sliding Away (V) (Errata 2)]], 20 April 2022): Players Committee card image, 20 April 2022: 0 side [[:File:V12-D-slipslidingaway-E1-2022.png]] ([https://github.com/swccgpc/holotable/blob/2640d50/Images-HT/starwars/Virtual12-Dark/hires/slipslidingaway.png Holotable commit 2640d50 “Set 18 and errata”], mark “E1”).
